subject: Verdant AI - request for service credit eligibility and next steps
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@verdant.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Kline <tom.kline@verdant.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service disruption May 8 — asking about credit eligibility

Hi Aditya,

We had a multi-hour degradation of inference throughput on May 8 that affected our production feature (user recommendations). I've attached Verdant's uptime export for the window (uptime_report_20270508.csv). Our billing/accounting team wants to understand whether this incident qualifies for an SLA credit under Section 4.2 of our contract (reserved capacity, 99.9% per-month uptime).

Key info:
- Incident id we were given: IR-2027-05-08-44
- Impact window observed: 2027-05-08 02:40 - 2027-05-08 06:05 UTC (partial recovery sequence after 04:30)
- Estimated user-facing errors: ~1.8% of requests for the affected route during the window

Can you confirm whether Verdant is eligible for a credit, and share how you calculate the credit amount and how it will be applied on our invoice? We prefer an invoice adjustment rather than a refund.

Thanks — appreciate a quick acknowledgement while you investigate.

Best,
Maria Garcia
Head of Ops, Verdant AI

Attachment: uptime_report_20270508.csv
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@verdant.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service disruption May 8 — asking about credit eligibility

Hi Maria — thanks for flagging this and for the uptime export. I’m looping in Laura from Finance and Hannah from Reliability so we can triage eligibility and prepare a calculation.

Prelim notes:
- We have the incident record (IR-2027-05-08-44) and are finalizing the timeline/impact buckets.
- If the verified customer-facing uptime for the billing period drops below the SLA threshold, you’re typically eligible for a pro-rata credit computed against the affected service tier.

Action plan:
1) Hannah will confirm the verified impact window and whether any requests were served by fallback model variants (affects weighting).
2) Laura will draft a credit calculation and confirm how it will be reflected on your next invoice (invoice adjustment or credit memo).
3) I’ll share the postmortem PDF once it’s cleared for customer distribution and we’ll propose a credit amount.

Expect an update by EOD Monday (May 10). If you have additional logs or request IDs you want us to correlate, please attach them.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Verdant AI - incident timeline confirmation (IR-2027-05-08-44)

Aditya / Laura — I reviewed the runtime traces and routing logs for the Verdant org. Findings summary:
- Root cause: a regression in the KV-cache eviction path triggered by an edge case in concurrent warm-start logic after a short backend failover; fix deployed at 2027-05-08 04:12 UTC.
- User-facing degradation: 02:40 - 04:12 UTC (requests saw increased latency and ~1.8% error rate). Post-fix there was a recovery window with degraded tail latency until 06:05 UTC for long-running sessions.
- Some requests were served from a read-only fallback which reduced error surface but added latency; that reduces eligible token-weighting by ~12% for the affected route.

I’ve placed detailed timing and percent-of-traffic buckets into the internal workbook (credit_calc_workbook_aditya_v1.xlsx). Laura — you can use the adjusted exposure metric for the credit math.

Hannah
Principal Reliability Engineer

Attachment: credit_calc_workbook_aditya_v1.xlsx
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@verdant.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed credit calculation and issuance approach

Hi Maria — thanks for your patience. Based on Hannah’s verified impact windows and the contract SLA language, here is the proposed calculation and issuance path:

1) Eligible exposure: 2.8 hours of reduced availability between 02:40 - 04:12 UTC (full error window) plus graded exposure through 06:05 UTC. After weighting for fallback traffic, the net eligible exposure is 2.45 hours for the billing period.

2) Credit formula (per contract): monthly_service_fee * (eligible_minutes_impacted / total_minutes_in_month) * service_tier_multiplier.
- For Verdant (monthly reserved capacity fee = $48,000).
- eligible_minutes_impacted = 2.45 * 60 = 147 minutes.
- total_minutes_in_month (May) = 31 * 24 * 60 = 44,640 minutes.
- service_tier_multiplier = 1.0 (reserved capacity).

3) Preliminary credit: $48,000 * (147 / 44,640) = $158.10 (rounded to $158).

4) Issuance options:
- Standard: Credit memo applied to next invoice (preferred).
- Alternate: If Verdant requires a one-off non-invoice adjustment (e.g., accounting constraints), we can issue a DocuSign acceptance for a manual credit.

5) Approval path: Finance sign-off (Laura) + Ops acknowledgement (Hannah) + Sales approval for amounts >$1,000 (Stephanie). Since this is < $1,000, Laura can approve without exec sign-off.

I’m attaching the workbook and a redwood postmortem (customer-facing) draft. Please confirm whether the invoice adjustment is acceptable and whether Verdant wants a DocuSign approval route.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Finance Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit_calc_workbook_aditya_v1.xlsx, redwood_postmortem_20270508.pdf
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@verdant.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed credit calculation and issuance approach

Confirmed — finance approval granted for issuance as a credit memo on next invoice. No additional internal approvals required.

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Revenue Operations

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@verdant.ai>, payments@verdant.ai
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: SLA credit for May 8 incident (IR-2027-05-08-44) — confirmation and next steps

Hi Maria / Verdant AP team — following our internal review, we confirm Verdant is eligible for a service credit for the May 8 incident. Summary and next steps below.

Summary:
- Incident: IR-2027-05-08-44 (root cause and mitigation detailed in attached postmortem).
- Verified eligible exposure (weighted): 147 minutes (2.45 hours).
- Credit calculated per contract: $158 (rounded).

How it will be applied:
- We will issue a credit memo for $158 and apply it against Verdant’s next Redwood invoice. Expected posting on the invoice generated for June 1 billing cycle.
- If Verdant requires a signed acceptance prior to the adjustment (company policy), we can prepare a short acceptance form via DocuSign — please advise which you prefer.

Attachments included: redwood_postmortem_20270508.pdf (customer-facing), credit_calc_workbook_aditya_v1.xlsx (detailed math), uptime_report_20270508.csv (customer data).

Please confirm acceptance of the invoice adjustment or request the DocuSign route and we’ll send the link within one business day.

Thanks for working through this with us — we’ll continue to monitor and Hannah will follow up with any additional mitigations we've rolled into the runtime to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_postmortem_20270508.pdf, credit_calc_workbook_aditya_v1.xlsx, uptime_report_20270508.csv
